query: Which checks should I run after a tiny bug fix?

samples.document: For a small code fix, run the affected test suite first; broad solution tests are needed only when the change crosses project boundaries.
Leave completed changes uncommitted for review. Stage, commit, or push Git changes only when the user explicitly requests it.
Use FindSymbolAsync for C# symbol discovery; plain text search misses overloads and inherited members.
Correction: release deadlines use America/New_York local time, not UTC.
Keep code comments concise and explain the reason for surprising behavior, without repeating what the next line does.
On Windows, use PowerShell LiteralPath when handling filenames containing brackets or wildcard characters.
Keep confidential repository notes on the local machine; do not send them to external hosted model services.
Public documentation drafts may use hosted models. The restriction on cloud processing applies to confidential repository notes.
